# Factoring fun!

## Loading libraries and importing data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(praise)
```

```{r}
intd_datadict <- read_csv(here("Week_09","Data","intertidal_data_dictionary.csv"))
intd_lat <- read_csv(here("Week_09","Data","intertidaldata_latitude.csv"))
intd_data <- read_csv(here("Week_09","Data","intertidaldata.csv"))
```

### Viewing each dataset to decide which to work with
```{r}
view(intd_datadict)
view(intd_lat)
view(intd_data)
```

## Make a bar plot of site by latitude
```{r}
intd_lat |>
  ggplot(aes(x=fct_reorder(Site,Latitude),y=Latitude)) +  # Make a basic barplot, then reorder by latitude in descending order so the northernmost site is highest
  geom_col() +
  labs(title="Eastern Pacific Intertidal Sampling Locations by Latitude",
       x = "Intertidal Sampling Sites") +                          # Add plot title and fix axes names
  coord_flip() +                                                   # Flip the barplot so plot reads northern to southern latitudes from top to bottom
  scale_y_continuous(position="right") +                           # Shift y axis to the right so it is on top when the plot flips
  theme_minimal()
```
## Let's make a map, because I love OR and CA and want to practice mapping
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
west_coast_best_coast <- map_data("state") |>
  filter(region == "oregon" | region == "california")
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = west_coast_best_coast,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "darkcyan",
    color = "black") +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(title = "Map of Oregon and California",
       x="Longitude",
       y="Latitude") +
  theme_minimal()
```
